'''Meshgan Mohammed Al-Awar''' {{Lang|ar|مشكان العور}} (1968 - July 2020, ~52 yrs. old) was a renowned Emirati chemical researcher. She was the first Emirati woman to specialize in chemistry and the first to work as a chemistry teacher. She contributed to the development of the unified chemistry curriculum across the countries of the [[Gulf Cooperation Council]] (GCC) countries.

[[UNESCO]] selected her as co-chair for social responsibility on the [[International Advisory Council for Sustainability Development]] in the UNESCO office in Hong Kong. She was the first Emirati and the first Arab woman to hold such a position at this level within the organization.

== Biography ==
Al-Awar was born in [[Dubai]], into an academic family.<ref>[https://www.albayan.ae/across-the-uae/news-and-reports/2020-07-27-1.3922769 جريدة البيان__الموت يُغيّب مشكان العور.. رائدة الكيمياء الإماراتية] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200731012602/https://www.albayan.ae/across-the-uae/news-and-reports/2020-07-27-1.3922769|date=July 31, 2020}}</ref> She earned a Bachelor of Science in Geology and Chemistry from the [[United Arab Emirates University]] in 1990, and a PhD in [[Polymer]] Science (Physical Chemistry) from the [[University of Wales]] in the United Kingdom in 1996. 

She was director of research and remote sensing studies<ref>{{Cite web |title= |url=https://www.wam.ae/en/article/hsyidq2f-uae-woman-scientist-list-left-mars}}</ref> at the [[Dubai Police Academy]] between 2012 and 2020, and head of the Women's Police Department for Community Service in Dubai.<ref>{{Cite web |last=البيان |title=مشكان العور تجتاز برنامجاً علمياً حول «القيادة بالأزمات والكوارث» |url=https://www.albayan.ae/across-the-uae/accidents/2013-04-21-1.1866804 |access-date=2025-09-09 |website=www.albayan.ae |language=ar}}</ref> She was also a visiting professor at the Remote Sensing Research Center at [[Boston University]].<ref>[https://mawso3a.net/%D9%85%D9%86-%D9%87%D9%8A-%D9%85%D8%B4%D9%83%D8%A7%D9%86-%D8%A7%D9%84%D8%B9%D9%88%D8%B1-%D9%88%D9%8A%D9%83%D9%8A%D8%A8%D9%8A%D8%AF%D9%8A%D8%A7/ من هي مشكان العور؟] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200731011125/https://mawso3a.net/من-هي-مشكان-العور-ويكيبيديا/|date=July 31, 2020}}</ref>

The last positions Dr. Mashkan Al-Awar held were Secretary-General of the Zayed International Foundation for the Environment, and Advisor for the Academic and Training Sector at Dubai Police.<ref name=":0" />

Al-Awar died on 26 July 2020.<ref>[https://www.emaratalyoum.com/local-section/other/2020-07-28-1.1380590 رحيل «المعلمة الأولى» صاحبة المقام العلمي.. مشكان العور] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200729054126/https://www.emaratalyoum.com/local-section/other/2020-07-28-1.1380590|date=July 29, 2020}}</ref> She was married and had four children.<ref name=":0">{{Cite web |last=الخطيب |first=محمود |title=زهرة الخليج - مشكان العور رائدة الكيمياء الإماراتية |url=https://www.zahratalkhaleej.ae/article/4125438/%D9%85%D8%B4%D9%83%D8%A7%D9%86-%D8%A7%D9%84%D8%B9%D9%88%D8%B1-%D8%B1%D8%A7%D8%A6%D8%AF%D8%A9-%D8%A7%D9%84%D9%83%D9%8A%D9%85%D9%8A%D8%A7%D8%A1-%D8%A7%D9%84%D8%A5%D9%85%D8%A7%D8%B1%D8%A7%D8%AA%D9%8A%D8%A9 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220927211648/https://www.zahratalkhaleej.ae/article/4125438/%D9%85%D8%B4%D9%83%D8%A7%D9%86-%D8%A7%D9%84%D8%B9%D9%88%D8%B1-%D8%B1%D8%A7%D8%A6%D8%AF%D8%A9-%D8%A7%D9%84%D9%83%D9%8A%D9%85%D9%8A%D8%A7%D8%A1-%D8%A7%D9%84%D8%A5%D9%85%D8%A7%D8%B1%D8%A7%D8%AA%D9%8A%D8%A9 |archive-date=2022-09-27 |access-date=2025-09-09 |website=زهرة الخليج |language=ar}}</ref>

== Research and memberships ==
In 2005, she represented the United Arab Emirates in the Arab Women in Science and Technology Network. She was also selected as a Middle East regional expert to contribute to scenario development for the [[United Nations]] Environment Programme’s Fourth Global Environment Outlook (GEO-4) report. She previously served as the head of the Environmental Research and Studies Center at the Zayed International Prize for the Environment.She was a member of the Environmental Committee of the [[Humaid bin Rashid Al Nuaimi III|Hamid Bin Rashid Al Nuaimi]] Foundation for Development and Human Advancement in [[Ajman]]. Additionally, she served on the Scientific Committee of the Dubai International Conference on [[Desertification]], as well as the Dubai International Conference on Water Resources Management in the Third Millennium (2002).<ref name=":0" />

== Awards ==
She won several awards, including:<ref>{{Cite news |last=amal.monther |date=2016-03-21 |title=الدكتورة مشكان العور |url=https://www.sayidaty.net/awards/content/%D8%A7%D9%84%D8%AF%D9%83%D8%AA%D9%88%D8%B1%D8%A9-%D9%85%D8%B4%D9%83%D8%A7%D9%86-%D8%A7%D9%84%D8%B9%D9%88%D8%B1 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230204093540/https://www.sayidaty.net/awards/content/%D8%A7%D9%84%D8%AF%D9%83%D8%AA%D9%88%D8%B1%D8%A9-%D9%85%D8%B4%D9%83%D8%A7%D9%86-%D8%A7%D9%84%D8%B9%D9%88%D8%B1 |archive-date=2023-02-04 |access-date=2025-09-09 |work=جائزة سيدتي للإبداع والتميز |language=ar}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=رحيل العالمة الإماراتية مشكان العور – مؤسسة سلطان بن علي العويس الثقافية |url=https://www.alowais.com/%D8%B1%D8%AD%D9%8A%D9%84-%D8%A7%D9%84%D8%B9%D8%A7%D9%84%D9%85%D8%A9-%D8%A7%D9%84%D8%A5%D9%85%D8%A7%D8%B1%D8%A7%D8%AA%D9%8A%D8%A9-%D9%85%D8%B4%D9%83%D8%A7%D9%86-%D8%A7%D9%84%D8%B9%D9%88%D8%B1/ |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240830015219/https://www.alowais.com/%D8%B1%D8%AD%D9%8A%D9%84-%D8%A7%D9%84%D8%B9%D8%A7%D9%84%D9%85%D8%A9-%D8%A7%D9%84%D8%A5%D9%85%D8%A7%D8%B1%D8%A7%D8%AA%D9%8A%D8%A9-%D9%85%D8%B4%D9%83%D8%A7%D9%86-%D8%A7%D9%84%D8%B9%D9%88%D8%B1/ |archive-date=2024-08-30 |access-date=2025-09-09 |website=www.alowais.com |language=ar}}</ref>

* In 1999, she won the Distinguished Government Performance Award in the “Distinguished Government Employee” category.
* Winner of [[Sayidaty|Sayidaty Award]] for Creativity and Excellence in Science and Medicine.
* Distinguished Woman Award at the 3rd Middle East Community Service Awards.
* UNESCO Hong Kong awarded Al-Awar the "Women Leaders in Community Service" award in 2018, for her contributions to achieving the United Nations 2030 Agenda for Sustainable Development Goals.
